title: Entitlement Epoching and SIEM Uptake Playbook
content:
Purpose
This playbook proposes a practical design and rollout approach for capturing authorization state transitions as first-class artifacts ("entitlement epochs") and for exporting those artifacts into a compact SIEM-friendly timeline. The goal is to enable deterministic evidence reconstruction for audits and to accelerate automated evidence ingestion for SOC/Observability teams while minimizing runtime overhead.

Background and motivation
- Current RBAC telemetry at Redwood is event-oriented (grants, revokes, token usage) but lacks a compact, reconstructable snapshot sequence for a principal+resource combo. Auditors ask for "state at time T" proofs which we struggle to assemble from high-volume event logs.
- We also need a stable export format for entitlement evidence that SIEMs can ingest with bounded storage and query cost.
- Existing docs cover attribute-driven access catalogs and entitlement tagging; this playbook focuses on an orthogonal operational primitive: epoched snapshots + diffs + export policies.

Key concepts (definitions)
- Entitlement Epoch: an immutable snapshot of all effective permissions for a tenant/principal scope at a defined logical time boundary (epoch id + timestamp). Not every event creates an epoch — epochs are generated on policy changes, role composition updates, or periodic checkpoints.
- Delegation Snapshot: a compact representation of transitive delegations (who delegated to whom, scope, TTL) at an epoch boundary.
- Compact SIEM Timeline Format (CSTF): a line-delimited, gzipped JSON-lines export tailored for SIEM ingestion. Each record is one of: epoch_metadata, entitlement_record (per principal), delegation_delta, or verification_manifest.
- Evidence Token: a signed pointer (short-lived JWT) that references a particular epoch and verification_manifest for external auditors or downstream systems to retrieve or verify evidence.

Design overview
1) Generation rules
  - Epoch triggers: (a) role/permission model change (PR merged), (b) manual snapshot trigger (security team), (c) scheduled checkpoint (default 24h), (d) pre-rollout snapshot before major infra changes.
  - When triggered, the entitlement service performs a breadth-first evaluation for tenant-scoped principals and emits entitlement_records only for principals with non-empty permissions (sparse encoding).
  - Delegation snapshots are emitted as separate records to keep entitlement_records small. Delegation_deltas describe additions/removals since the last epoch.

2) Storage and retention
  - Epochs stored in the entitlement-store (immutable blobs) with retention policies: 90d hot, 540d cold. Index: (tenant_id, epoch_id, start_ts).
  - For cost-sensitive tenants, we support "compact horizons": retain only the last N epochs + periodic monthly checkpoints.

3) SIEM export (CSTF)
  - Each CSTF export is a gzipped JSONL file with filename pattern: tenant_epoch_{tenant}_{epoch_id}_{ts}.cstf.gz.
  - Records are schema-minimized (no repeated role definitions) and use id references to shared objects (role_id, resource_class_id). The export includes a verification_manifest with a content hash and signing metadata.
  - For downstream SIEMs that cannot import full epochs, we provide a staged ingest option: ingest only verification_manifests + pointers and fetch entitlement_records on-demand via the Evidence API.

4) Evidence automation pipeline
  - Ingest step: entitlement-store -> transform service (minify + compress) -> signer service (KMS/HSM) -> S3 export bucket (cross-region replication) -> SIEM connector (push/pull).
  - Automation ensures exports are atomic per-epoch and that verification manifests have deterministic hashes.
  - Alerts: failed export, signer failures, bucket permission anomalies. Tickets open automatically to infra on SLO breach.

5) Authorization verification flow (for audits)
  - Auditor receives Evidence Token -> calls Evidence API to retrieve verification_manifest -> checks S3 object hash and signature -> optionally requests selective entitlement_records for sampled principals -> verifier can replay policy evaluation deterministically within a sandbox to validate the snapshot.

Rollout plan (phased)
Phase 0 — Prep (2–3 weeks)
  - Finalize CSTF schema and signer contract (security sign-off).
  - Create entitlement-store TTL and tagging defaults.
  - Run a small pilot for internal tenants (security, infra).
  - Tickets: SEC-EP-001 (schema freeze), INFRA-EP-002 (S3 staging).

Phase 1 — Internal canary (4–6 weeks)
  - Enable epoching for internal tenants only. Generate daily epochs (no SIEM push).
  - Run reconciliation job: attempt to reconstruct access decisions from epoch + policy engine and compare to live enforcement logs for sampled requests.
  - Measure pipeline costs: typical epoch size, gzipped export size, avg time to generate and sign.

Phase 2 — Customer pilots (8–12 weeks)
  - Offer opt-in to a set of pilot customers via customer success and security review. Enable CSTF export to their SIEM endpoints.
  - Add selective retention controls via Console (Dedicated/Private customers can set retention, compact horizons).
  - Gather feedback on schema utility, SIEM ingestion compatibility, and verification latency.

Phase 3 — Gradual ramp + enforcement (3 months)
  - Default epoching enabled for all tenants with conservative schedule (24h). Export to internal SIEM while allowing opt-out for external push.
  - Enforcement: request-level audit traces will reference the latest epoch id in log metadata.

Operational SLAs and telemetry
- Generation time SLO: 95th percentile epoch generation for a medium tenant < 4 minutes.
- CSTF export push latency to SIEM: 99th percentile < 10 minutes from epoch completion.
- Verification API availability: 99.9% monthly uptime.
- Telemetry to track: epoch_size_bytes, entitlement_record_count, delegation_delta_count, export_failures, signer_errors, fetch_latency.

Testing and validation
- Deterministic replay tests: run 1000 sampled principals through local policy evaluator to confirm identical decisions to those captured in the epoch.
- Fuzz tests: random role graph mutations and delegation churn to validate snapshot correctness and delta generation.
- Load tests: simulate large enterprise tenant with 100k principals and measure epoch generation time and export size.

Security considerations
- Signed manifests (KMS) to prevent tampering. Keys rotated per key-rotation policy and recorded in verification_manifest.
- Least-privilege for signer and export services. Only the security team can trigger ad-hoc epochs for customer tenants.
- Redaction rules: exports strip sensitive resource attributes (PII) by default unless tenant opts in and completes DPA/ROI checks.

Open questions / decision points
- Epoch frequency tradeoff: daily vs. event-triggered (cost vs. forensic granularity). Proposal: hybrid default (daily + on-policy-change).
- Canonical replay environment: where should the deterministic policy evaluator live for auditors? Consider a hermetic service with pinned model versions.
- Delegation TTL semantics and expiry handling across epochs; should expired delegations be retained as tombstones?

Action items (next 2 weeks)
- SEC: freeze CSTF schema v0.1 (owner: Maya) — due 2025-11-11.
- ENG-AuthZ: prototype epoch blob format and signer integration (owner: Ethan) — spike due 2025-11-18.
- OBS: create Grafana dashboards for epoch metrics and export failures (owner: Sofia) — due 2025-11-20.

Notes and references
- Related: attribute-driven access catalogue and audit-export proposals (see linked Confluence).
- Quick sketch: sample CSTF record examples are in the attached gist (link in linked_artifacts).

Appendix: informal engineer notes (scratch)
- We should avoid full materialization for tiny tenants; use delta-only epochs for tenants with >1M principals.
- Consider compressing role definitions separately and referencing via role_shas to reduce repetition.
- TODO: evaluate protobuf vs JSONL for CSTF transport; JSONL is more consumable for SIEMs today.

This document is an operational playbook — not final. Feedback requested from ENG-SRE, ENG-AUTHZ, OBS, and Customer Success on pilot readiness and retention defaults.
